text: Ninh Bình estimates 11.43 per cent growth as Deputy PM calls for decisive action

NINH BÌNH - Deputy Prime Minister Nguyễn Văn Thắng on November 19 asked authorities in Ninh Bình to act decisively to ensure that full-year economic growth meets or exceeds its target, after the northern province reported estimated growth of more than 11 per cent for 2026.
The deputy PM made the request during a working session with the provincial government on measures to drive double-digit growth and on the province's main tasks for the period ahead.
He commended Ninh Bình's efforts and socio-economic results.
He said the province should closely monitor its growth scenario for the fourth quarter so it could respond promptly to any problems.
The senior official also said Ninh Bình should concentrate on disbursing public investment and finish resolving the 157 outstanding projects for which solutions have already been identified.

Trần Song Tùng, deputy chairman of the People's Committee of Ninh Bình, told the meeting that the province's gross regional domestic product, measured at 2020 constant prices, was estimated to grow 11.43 per cent this year.

He said that budget revenue was expected to exceed VNĐ80 trillion (US$3.1 billion), or 114 per cent of the amount the central government assigned to Ninh Bình, and that the province had met 38 of its 39 socio-economic development targets.
As of November 10, the province had disbursed nearly VNĐ16.6 trillion ($646 million) in public investment, or 47.2 per cent of its plan.
Provincial authorities said they were addressing each bottleneck in turn and were determined to fulfil the plan in full.
Ninh Bình still has 357 projects facing difficulties.
Of the total, 96 have been resolved and solutions have been identified for 157, which the province aims to settle within 2026.
A further 68 are under review, and 36 require support from the central government.

The province leader also reported that Ninh Bình had completed, on schedule, 150 of the 158 tasks set out under Politburo Resolution 57 on breakthroughs in science, technology, innovation and national digital transformation.

It has brought into operation NinhBinh-S, a smart monitoring and operations centre that applies digital technology, and is developing shared data warehouse platforms and a cybersecurity monitoring centre.
Ninh Bình has also completed revisions to its provincial master plan for 2021-2030.
The revised plan will form the basis for organising development around multiple growth poles and centres.
Looking further ahead, the deputy PM said Ninh Bình needed to renew its growth model, with science and technology, innovation, digital transformation and the green transition as its main drivers.

He asked the province to implement the revised master plan effectively and prepare zoning plans for its urban areas, including a study of transit-oriented development around the high-speed railway station.
The leader asked Ninh Bình to prioritise resources for key projects that strengthen regional connectivity and to remove infrastructure bottlenecks.

The projects he cited were the TD07 longitudinal road and the bridge over the Red River linking the province with Hưng Yên, the first phase of the Hà Nam-Nam Định Expressway and the Ninh Bình-Hải Phòng Expressway.
He called for close coordination with the relevant agencies on the North-South high-speed railway so that site clearance and resettlement stay on schedule, and for a secure supply of materials.
On digital transformation, the deputy PM said the province should implement its digital transformation scheme for 2026-2030 and develop its digital and data infrastructure.
He said Ninh Bình should also build and connect shared and sector-specific databases, and work with telecommunications companies to extend 5G coverage across the province.
Deputy PM Thắng also asked the province to keep prices and inflation under tight control.

He asked Ninh Bình to complete periodic health checks and free screening for all residents in 2026, linked to electronic health records, with particular attention to communes and wards where coverage is low.
Ninh Bình should also closely monitor labour relations, wages and year-end bonuses at industrial parks and streamline the two-tier local government system, he said.
He added that the province should introduce key performance indicator (KPI) assessments for provincial departments and agencies, tied to how officials are evaluated and assigned. - VNS
